card.name: Pronouns in old-style prose
card.fires_on: Pronouns such as this, it, I, you and the word subject, at the start of a clause in old-fashioned or 19th-century scientific and literary prose. They usually refer back to a species, a work or a topic just described.

modes.label: Sentence-opening This/It
modes.description: This or It begins a sentence that refers back to something just described, such as a species or a shot.
modes.example: <<This>> species is most intimately allied to the House

modes.label: Mid-sentence this/you/subject
modes.description: A pronoun or the word subject appears inside a clause in archaic essay prose.
modes.example: We shall divide the<< subject>> into four Sections; namely, first,
